operations.evidence: Monthly API crime-data refresh and the required currency check were recorded.
Monthly refresh was not represented as complete force-product coverage or parcel timing.
The ISO date was preserved as a latest-data month whose day component is documented as irrelevant.
The day was not interpreted as an extraction or incident date.
The explicit year-month list of available street-level datasets was recorded.
A listed month was not treated as proof that every field or locality is complete.
Month-specific force IDs supplying stop-search data were recorded.
A missing force was treated as unavailable data rather than zero searches.
The default latest month can contain no data for a requested force and availability lookup was required.
An empty default response was not interpreted as no stop-search activity.
Stop-search coordinates were recorded as anonymised approximations rather than exact locations.
Approximate coordinates were forbidden from exact parcel joins.
The 23 July 2026 England-and-Wales outcome-release edition and year-ending March 2026 scope were recorded.
Publication date was not substituted for offence or outcome dates.
The transition from detections to the broader outcomes framework and supply since April 2014 were recorded.
Pre-framework and current series were not treated as directly interchangeable.
The framework's no-favoured-outcome and appropriate-disposal purpose was recorded.
Outcome codes were not converted into an ordinal success scale.
Monthly checks for large or unusual changes in offences outcomes and cancelled records were recorded.
A passed aggregate check was not represented as record-level audit proof.
Checks for data supplied against obsolete offence classifications were recorded.
Classification validity was not represented as proof of correct local recording.
Long-term offence and outcome trend comparisons used to identify monthly outliers were recorded.
Trend conformity was not represented as correctness and structural changes remained possible.
Cautions assigned to rape offences and referral to Force Crime Registrars were recorded.
A validation query was not automatically labelled a confirmed error.
Outcome 17 compatibility with offence time limits was recorded as a monthly validation rule.
Framework-specific validation did not replace force record review.
Outcome 7 was restricted by validation to cannabis or khat offence scope.
A valid code combination was not treated as a local safety indicator.
Force investigation explanation and corrected resubmission pathways were recorded.
Force production QA was not represented as independent inspection and later revisions remained possible.
HODH record-level detail and its expanded analytical opportunity were recorded.
Record-level Home Office supply was not represented as public parcel evidence or uniform fields.
A small number of forces using monthly aggregate Crimsec4 returns was recorded.
Aggregate returns were not treated as equivalent in detail to HODH records.
Crimsec4 notifiable-offence scope including jury-triable and specified summary offences was recorded.
The notifiable list was not represented as all police-known incidents.
Crimsec4 outcomes were assigned to application month rather than original offence month.
Monthly outcome and offence volumes were not treated as matched cohorts.
The April 2025 to March 2026 interview window was recorded separately from occurrence timing.
Interview month was not treated as incident month and overlapping recall periods were retained.
